name: Tsukiji
tagline: Toranomon in 7 minutes and Tokyo in 10 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000.
summary: The station is in Chuo City, where Tokyo Metro run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 11 minutes to Otemachi, 23 minutes to Shinjuku, 22 minutes to Shibuya and 20 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. The station stands 2.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 0.9 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 2.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 2.1 m to 3 m, a difference of 0.9 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 3 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is about average for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 9 clinics and 5 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 聖路加国際病院, about 7 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 国立がん研究センター中央病院, about 11 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line run through it. Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line also call here. Both lines are run by Tokyo Metro, so a fault affecting that company can stop them together.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line runs at 163% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 三ノ輪→入谷, which this station is not on. Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line runs at 153%. Its busiest stretch is 東池袋→護国寺, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥140,000 to ¥150,000 and 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. 1LDK ¥230,000 to ¥240,000 and 2LDK ¥320,000 to ¥330,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Tsukiji, but Higashi-Ginza is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Tsukiji. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Tsukiji. One-room rents run about ¥16,000 higher.

neighbours.lead: Hatchobori is ahead on how easy the shopping is, but Tsukiji is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Tsukiji. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Tsukiji.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
People who want a park close by
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
noiseSources: The 首都高速都心環状線(第2通行帯) viaduct runs just outside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
新大橋通り (2 lanes each way) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 2 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 6 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. The choice of connections is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are some of the most heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: Whether a flat faces the road changes what you hear indoors.
